title: The doctrines, looking back
tomorrow: the disciples never asked Jesus how to preach. what did they ask?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the feasts: a year that turns through the life of Jesus, and a Sunday that comes round every week. The circle turns. Today, what the circle is about.

A crowded room goes quiet, then everyone starts the same song at once, and one shaking voice disappears into all the others. In Mark, a father brings his son to Jesus and begs for help. Jesus tells him all things are possible to him that believeth. And the father cries out, with tears: “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.” Both at once, in one breath. And he isn't sent away.
screen: `ONE SHAKING VOICE.` → `LORD, I BELIEVE.` → `HELP THOU MINE UNBELIEF.`

segments.voice: That father is a good door into the doctrines, the big teachings Christians hold. The Trinity: one God, Father, Son and Spirit, the name Jesus sends his friends to baptize in, “in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.” The incarnation: God come close in a human life. The cross: Paul passes on “that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures.” Grace: “For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.” And hope: the resurrection, and a world made new. Churches gathered these into creeds short enough to say aloud. The old English prayer book begins the Apostles' Creed: “I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth.” Orthodox, Catholic and Protestant churches explain grace and the Spirit in their own ways, and some churches don't recite creeds at all. Now listen to how a creed sounds. When a congregation says one, it says it together, out loud, at one pace. Some Christians say that on days they can't manage I believe alone, the we carries them, the way the father brought half a belief, and his son was healed.
screen: `TRINITY AND INCARNATION.` · `CROSS, GRACE, HOPE.` · `CREEDS SHORT ENOUGH TO SAY.` · `ONE ROOM, ONE PACE.` · then, large: `WE BELIEVE.`

segments.voice: Put a hand flat on your chest and say one line out loud, slowly, the way a room says it together: I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth. Feel the words hum under your hand. If that line isn't yours, say the father's instead, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief, or simply hum one long note and feel it there.
The doctrines. Trinity, incarnation, cross, grace and hope, gathered into creeds that a whole room says together.
The line to keep: we believe, and the we can carry a shaking I. Said out loud, day twenty-four of the summit.
